gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 identifies the same failed conversion in the main approximation theorem: Parseval makes the Fourier L2 error equal to the Frobenius residual, but the proof incorrectly bounds it by the maximum-entry residual. It explicitly notes that no one-entry restriction applies, gives the missing dimension factor, and carries the defect into the dependent CUR corollary.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Fourier L2 error is exactly the Frobenius norm of B=A-EF*, whereas the available theorem controls only the maximum norm. Without a sparsity or single-entry hypothesis, replacing the Frobenius norm by the maximum norm omits a factor up to sqrt((2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)), invalidating the dimension-free epsilon||A||_2 term and the dependent CUR bound.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof uses the wrong norm conversion: Parseval gives the exact Fourier L2/Frobenius identity, and a max-entry bound cannot serve as a dimension-free upper bound without a one-entry restriction.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the exact Parseval/Frobenius identity, explains that Frobenius can exceed the maximum-entry norm by the dimension square-root factor, and rejects the asserted L2-to-max-norm inequality in general.

component_coverage.gold_component: The omitted factor invalidates the dimension-free approximation term and propagates to the maximal-volume CUR corollary; the repair is to include the square-root dimension factor and update the affected statements.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies failure of the dimension-free epsilon||A||_2 guarantee, applies the same false transfer to Corollary 4.2, and specifies replacing the max-norm input with a Frobenius or spectral bound and revising the rank/error trade-off.
